headline: UK-based Farhaan Ali set to make Bangladesh debut against Malaysia
summary: The winger is expected to start on the left wing as Bangladesh opens their FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign in Indonesia today.
details: Winger Farhaan Ali Wahid is set to make his international debut for Bangladesh in the Group A opener of the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia today.
The UK-based forward is expected to start on the left wing in head coach Thomas Dooley's 4-2-3-1 formation, with Fahamedul Islam on the right and Shamit Shome behind striker Rakib Hossain.
Rakib Hossain returns to the starting XI after having missed the clash against San Marino in June.
Bangladesh captain Jamal Bhuyan welcomed Farhaan's debut on social media, asking fans to keep the new player in their prayers.
In midfield, Hamza Choudhury and Sohel Rana Sr are expected to form the defensive partnership as Bangladesh faces a Malaysia side featuring 10 players of heritage descent from various countries.
The defensive line will likely consist of Zayyan Ahmed at left-back, Saad Uddin at right-back, and central defenders Tariq Kazi Raihan and Shakil Ahad Topu.
Goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon is expected to start the match, which kicks off at 3:00 PM Bangladesh time.
caption:
A new face in the squad! UK-based Farhaan Ali is set to make his Bangladesh debut today.

Winger Farhaan Ali Wahid is set to make his international debut for Bangladesh in the Group A opener of the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia today.

The UK-based forward is expected to start on the left wing in head coach Thomas Dooley's 4-2-3-1 formation, with Fahamedul Islam on the right and Shamit Shome behind striker Rakib Hossain.

Rakib Hossain returns to the starting XI after having missed the clash against San Marino in June.

Bangladesh captain Jamal Bhuyan welcomed Farhaan's debut on social media, asking fans to keep the new player in their prayers.

In midfield, Hamza Choudhury and Sohel Rana Sr are expected to form the defensive partnership as Bangladesh faces a Malaysia side featuring 10 players of heritage descent from various countries.

The defensive line will likely consist of Zayyan Ahmed at left-back, Saad Uddin at right-back, and central defenders Tariq Kazi Raihan and Shakil Ahad Topu.

Goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon is expected to start the match, which kicks off at 3:00 PM Bangladesh time.

headline: 70-80 injections: Former NCP member alleges torture in custody
summary: Gazi Sahlahuddin Tanvir claims he was given unknown injections, served rotten food, and suffered a stroke while held by police and prison authorities.
details: Gazi Sahlahuddin Tanvir, a former joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP), alleges he was subjected to extreme torture in police custody and prison between August 5 and September 15.

At a press conference in Dhaka, Tanvir claimed he was given at least 70 to 80 injections of unknown substances, which he says led to numbness in his limbs and a subsequent stroke diagnosis at Shaheed Zia Medical College Hospital.
He further alleged that he was served rotten food, denied prescribed medicines, and became paralyzed from the waist down after an MRI machine malfunctioned while he was inside.
Tanvir also claimed that men in plain clothes entered his prison vehicle and tortured him, mentioning the owners of Bashundhara Group, though he provided no evidence to support these specific claims.
Additionally, he alleged that Awami League leaders and activists received preferential treatment in prison, including access to phones and better food, while he was mistreated.
The victim claimed he was threatened that his family would be forcibly disappeared if he spoke out, but he decided to go public with his allegations of abuse.
caption:
“I was given at least 70-80 injections.”

A former NCP member alleges extreme torture and medical neglect in custody.

Gazi Sahlahuddin Tanvir, a former joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP), alleges he was subjected to extreme torture in police custody and prison between August 5 and September 15.

At a press conference in Dhaka, Tanvir claimed he was given at least 70 to 80 injections of unknown substances, which he says led to numbness in his limbs and a subsequent stroke diagnosis at Shaheed Zia Medical College Hospital.

He further alleged that he was served rotten food, denied prescribed medicines, and became paralyzed from the waist down after an MRI machine malfunctioned while he was inside.

Tanvir also claimed that men in plain clothes entered his prison vehicle and tortured him, mentioning the owners of Bashundhara Group, though he provided no evidence to support these specific claims.

Additionally, he alleged that Awami League leaders and activists received preferential treatment in prison, including access to phones and better food, while he was mistreated.

The victim claimed he was threatened that his family would be forcibly disappeared if he spoke out, but he decided to go public with his allegations of abuse.
